init_error.title: PlayGuard

onboarding.title: First steps
onboarding.headline: Three steps and the console is protected. A on a step does it.
onboarding.all_done: All set: the console is protected. Come back here any time from Tools & about.
onboarding.step_unlink: 4. Unlink the companion app (its next sync would undo this)
onboarding.step_alarm: {}. Turn the "Time's up" alarm back on (nothing says when time is up)
onboarding.at_start: Show at start-up while no PIN is set
onboarding.note: The PIN is the console's own; the limit is checked against the network clock, so it must be accurate.

play_timer.fw_too_old: The play timer needs firmware 21.0.0 or newer. The other tabs still work.

state.reached_alert: Today's limit is reached: the game is suspended.

play_timer.week_title_edit: This week's limits (A on a day changes it)
play_timer.quick_title_varies: Daily limit for every day (days differ now)
play_timer.per_day: A different limit for each day…
play_timer.suspend_warning: Already played today: {}. The game in progress is suspended as soon as parental controls are locked again.
play_timer.profiles_hint: A on a profile: apply it, edit its limits, rename or delete it.
play_timer.profile_bad_name: The name needs at least one Latin letter or digit.
play_timer.profile_replace: A profile named "{}" already exists. Replace it?
play_timer.bedtime_note: The bedtime alarm can only be changed from the companion app for now.
play_timer.alarm_on_body:
Turn the "Time's up" alarm back on?

When the play-time limit is reached, the console will show the alarm again, as it does by default.
play_timer.alarm_off_body:
Turn off the "Time's up" alarm?

When the play-time limit is reached, the console will no longer say so: the game is only suspended at the next lock.
play_timer.pause_body:
Pause today's countdown?

This uses a test command of the system. Use it only if you know why you need it.
play_timer.confirm_uniform: Set the limit to {} for every day?
play_timer.confirm_uniform_zero:
Set 0 minutes for every day?

That means no play at all. To turn the timer off instead, use "Remove the play-time limit".
play_timer.remove_body: Remove the play-time limit for every day?

gate.body: The play timer is counting down, so parental controls are unlocked temporarily first, with the stored PIN (you don't need to remember it).
gate.relock_auto: They are locked again right after the change.
gate.relock_manual: You can lock them again right after the change.

relock.body:
Parental controls are temporarily unlocked.

Lock them again now? The new limit applies as soon as they are locked.

Tip: if the limit is lower than the time already played today, the game is suspended right away.

restrictions.custom_only: To change these settings, choose the "Custom" level.
restrictions.confirm_org: Use {} age ratings? The age limit of the restriction level will then follow this organisation's ratings.
restrictions.note: These are the same settings as System Settings › Parental Controls.

clock.why: The play timer relies on the network clock. When it is inaccurate (a console that never reaches Nintendo's servers), set it here from a public time server.
clock.custom_header: NTP server name or IP address
clock.result_spread: Warning: the servers disagree by {} s.
clock.result_none: No server answered. Check the Internet connection.
clock.need_measure: Measure first (a measurement stays valid for 2 minutes).
clock.expired: The measurement is older than 2 minutes. Measure again.
clock.applied_ok: Network clock set. The system reports it as accurate.
clock.applied_pending: Network clock set and read back. The system does not report it as accurate yet.
clock.applied_refused: Not changed: turn on "Synchronise Clock via Internet" in System Settings › System › Date and Time first.
clock.applied_err: Could not set the network clock
clock.report_err_ask: The report of the clocks before the change could not be saved ({}). Set the network clock anyway?
clock.busy: Please wait for the current request.
clock.autosync_off_note: To set the network clock from it, first turn on "Synchronise Clock via Internet" in System Settings.
clock.start_off: The network clock is {} off (checked against {}). The play timer counts on it: see the Network clock tab.
clock.guided_body:
The network clock is inaccurate, and the play timer counts on it.

Measure the time against {} now? (The console must be online.) You will then be asked before the clock is set.
clock.guided_fine: The network clock is accurate: nothing to do.

pairing.unlink_body:
Unlink the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls companion app from this console?

Otherwise its next synchronisation overwrites the limits set here.
pairing.unlink_err: Could not unlink the companion app
pairing.note: While the console stays linked, the companion app overwrites the settings made here at its next synchronisation.

security.show_pin_body:
Show the PIN on screen?

Anyone looking at the screen can read it: make sure the child is not watching.
security.unlock_body:
Unlock parental controls temporarily?

Restrictions stay off until you lock them again (or until the console restarts).
security.delete_body:
Delete all parental controls?

This wipes the PIN, every restriction and the play-time limit. It cannot be undone, but a backup of the settings (not the PIN) is saved on the SD card first: Tools & about › Restore a backup.

pin_lock.title: Ask for the PIN

notes.off: Anyone who holds the console can change the settings here.
notes.changes: Anyone can look; changing something needs the PIN (asked again after 5 minutes). Locking again never asks.
notes.open: A lock screen until the PIN is entered. Locking again never asks.

pin_lock.no_pin: Set a PIN first (Set or change the PIN).
pin_lock.locked_body: Enter the parental-control PIN to open it.

console_lock.title: Console lock
console_lock.note_off: Sets every day's limit to 0, so a PIN is needed to start a game — a light lock without turning on age ratings or communication limits. It blocks starting games, not the HOME menu or System Settings. Needs a PIN on the console.
console_lock.note_on: Every day's limit is 0: a PIN is needed to play. Turning this off puts the previous limits back.
console_lock.needs_pin: Set a parental-control PIN first: without one, nothing stops a game from starting.
console_lock.on_body: Lock the console? Every day's play-time limit becomes 0, so the PIN is needed to start a game. The current limits are saved and come back when you turn this off.
console_lock.off_body: Unlock the console? The previous play-time limits are put back.
console_lock.blocks_change: The console lock is on: every day's limit stays at 0. Turn it off in Security & app first.

rescue.title: Recovery
rescue.section_actions: What would you like to do?
rescue.note: You reached this screen with the RESCUE file, so no PIN is asked here. Set a new PIN or remove the parental controls, then open PlayGuard.
rescue.note_failed: Recovery did not finish on its own. You can still try from here, or remove the SD card and edit the settings on a computer.
rescue.note_refused: Every parental control would have been deleted, but the request file could not be removed from the SD card, so it would have run again at every start. Remove it from a computer, then try again, or use the actions below.
rescue.request_kept: The {} file could not be removed from the SD card: until it is, the console is unlocked again at every start. Remove it from a computer.
rescue.note_deleted: Every parental control was removed, including the PIN. Open PlayGuard — you can set it up again from there whenever you like.
rescue.note_no_pin: No parental-control PIN was set, so there was nothing to unlock. You can set one here, then open PlayGuard.

outcome.unlocked: Parental controls were unlocked, so PlayGuard could open.
outcome.no_pin: There was no PIN to recover: no parental-control PIN is set.
outcome.refused: Nothing was deleted: the RESCUE file could not be removed from the SD card.

tools.export_note: Saved in {}. Attach it to a bug report. It never contains the PIN or the serial number.
tools.backup_note: Saves the restriction level, the custom settings, VR mode and the daily play-time limits in {}. The PIN is not saved.
tools.serial_note_emummc: This emuMMC uses the console's real serial number: if it goes online, Nintendo's servers see it. To blank it, set blank_prodinfo_emummc=1 in atmosphere/config/exosphere.ini and reboot (Atmosphère warns that blanking is not guaranteed to be safe).
tools.patches_note_files: The recommendation is now to use sys-patch: it patches the system at every boot, instead of files that must match each firmware version.
tools.patches_note_redundant: sys-patch is active: the sigpatch files ({}) are no longer needed.
tools.patches_note_not_at_boot: sys-patch is installed but not started at boot: turn it on in the sysmodules overlay (or create atmosphere/contents/420000000000000B/flags/boot2.flag), then reboot.
tools.patches_note_no_log: sys-patch left no log for this boot, so what it patched cannot be checked: set enable_logging=1 in config/sys-patch/config.ini, then reboot.
tools.patches_note_stale: sys-patch's log was written for firmware {} on {} storage: it did not run at this boot.
tools.patches_note_skipped: sys-patch is turned off for this storage: set {}=1 in config/sys-patch/config.ini, then reboot.
tools.patches_note_unpatched: sys-patch did not patch: {}. Update sys-patch for this firmware.
tools.auto_relock: Lock again automatically after a change
tools.extra_auto: Put the usual limit back the next day by itself
tools.clock_check: Check the network clock at start-up
tools.compat_ok_info: This firmware has been checked with PlayGuard: every feature is available.

dev.pt_block_intro:
Save the play-timer settings as they are now, as a reference?

Then change one setting in the Nintendo Switch Parental Controls app, let the console sync, and come back here: PlayGuard lists the values that changed. This is how the settings PlayGuard does not show yet (bedtime, alarm only or suspend the software) can be decoded.
